hero.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and pool party at country club
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Florida Lt. Governor's wife of running anonymous attack accounts
cards.body:
Two veteran communications staffers from Governor Ron DeSantis's administration have publicly alleged that Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, operated anonymous social media accounts to promote her husband's gubernatorial campaign while attacking the governor. Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both presented evidence linking the accounts to the Second Lady. The accounts were deactivated shortly after the accusations became public.

Pushaw shared information from Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing that the X account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email address similar to ones associated with Layla Collins. Florida Politics verified the connection through screenshots of two-factor authentication messages, which were triggered when someone attempted to access the account without the correct password. The screenshots displayed authentication messages sent to an email address with letters obscured and a phone number showing only the final digits. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said also appeared connected to Layla Collins. According to Pushaw, the account's posts consisted entirely of promoting Jay Collins and attacking individuals who refused to endorse him, including the governor.

Redfern corroborated the allegation, stating that "the FSUDude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number." Both accounts were deactivated after the two men publicly criticized them. Pushaw noted the apparent contradiction in Layla Collins serving on a state board appointed by the same governor whose account had called a coward. She questioned how someone with such important state duties would have time to maintain and post on multiple burner accounts so frequently. In her own posts, Pushaw emphasized that beyond the communication links, the account's content pattern suggested it existed primarily to advance her husband's political ambitions. "Account content is entirely comprised of two types of posts: Promoting Jay Collins, and attacking people who didn't endorse Jay, including the governor," Pushaw stated.

DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year, positioning the former state Senator to develop a statewide political profile. The governor has not endorsed a preferred candidate in the upcoming gubernatorial race and cannot seek a third term due to term limits. Redfern currently works for Attorney General James Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for governor. Florida Politics requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins regarding the allegations.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year for Facebook comment.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is challenging a judge's recommendation to reinstate a social studies teacher suspended last year for Facebook comments about conservative activist Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, who has taught at Spectrum Academy since 2009, was suspended after posting comments labeling Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation, contending that "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney maintains that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk constituted a "serious offense" and that his removal was appropriate.

However, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling in her order, which stated that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. She recommended Theobald receive back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald acknowledged writing the comments but stated they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald will be reinstated, with no clear timeline for a decision.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams prepare for Fourth of July boating surge
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats with medics on standby as hundreds of boaters take to local waterways for the holiday weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected to hit Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend, prompting Martin County Maritime Response Unit to prepare for the surge. Lt. Brett Harry said his team will station two boats with medics on standby in the north and south areas of Martin County to assist anyone in need. Harry noted the unit is prepared to handle everything from minor injuries like stubbed toes to serious medical emergencies including cardiac events and potential spinal injuries.

Harry urged boaters to take safety precautions by keeping their eyes on the water, designating a sober driver, and packing life vests, whistles and flotation devices. Among those preparing for the holiday weekend are boaters Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched Friday from Sandsprit Park in Martin County with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons said safety is their top priority when heading out on the water to celebrate.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Cord Byrd moves to keep St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark off ballot
cards.teaser: Five state employees gave sworn declarations that Paula Stark's treasurer never submitted required Form 6 paperwork before the June 12 qualifying deadline.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking Leon Circuit Court to keep St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark off the ballot, arguing she failed to submit required Form 6 paperwork before the June 12 deadline. Five state employees submitted sworn written declarations stating that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted Form 6 nor received it back when he submitted remaining paperwork in the final 30 minutes before the noon deadline. Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve said Stark was one of 12 candidates who did not properly turn in Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests. Half of those candidates corrected their problems and qualified. Three weeks after the deadline passed, Stark still has not submitted the form.

Reeve also cited Stark's history of paperwork violations, including a campaign finance report filed over one month late, reported excessive contributions, and an incorrect address on file. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. If Stark is removed from the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 will feature Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves with no other Republican candidates, though the district traditionally leans Democratic and covers Osceola and Orange counties. Byrd noted that ballots must be mailed to overseas military by July 4 and vote-by-mail ballots must be sent out July 9-16.

cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit deployed two boats with medics on standby Friday as hundreds of boaters launched into waterways for Fourth of July weekend .
cards.body:

The Martin County Maritime Response Unit has deployed two boats with medics on standby to assist boaters throughout the holiday period. Lt. Brett Harry said his team will patrol both north and south Martin County waters to help anyone in need, from minor injuries like stubbed toes to serious medical emergencies including cardiac events and potential spinal injuries.

Among those launching Friday from Sandsprit Park were boaters Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who set out with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons prioritized safety as they prepared for their holiday celebration. Lt. Harry encouraged all boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a sober driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Body of missing diver recovered near Fort Pierce Inlet
cards.teaser: The body of a missing diver was found on the Florida coast near Fort Pierce Inlet, according to deputies.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County deputies reported the recovery of a missing diver's body near Fort Pierce Inlet on the Florida coast. The discovery was made after the diver had been reported missing.

Deputies are handling the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the diver's death. The recovery took place along the Fort Pierce Inlet area.

hero.headline: Juno Beach residents demand fence at JB-7 beach access as trespassing complaints rise
hero.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons.
hero.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos in Juno Beach are calling for the town to reinstall a fence at the JB-7 public beach access point after trespassing complaints increased since the barrier was removed in 2023. The town took down the original fence for safety reasons, leaving only bushes to mark the boundary between the public walkway and private residential property. The missing barrier has created ongoing conflict between condo owners and beachgoers who use the public access route during peak summer months.

Lori Hill, a Colony resident, described the escalating problems that occur during summer season. "Lots of cars that just come at random, and then they just park on the spots there," Hill said. "Bushes are pushed back that they cut through those with their coolers and their fishing rods and lawn chairs and everything, and then they just park there all day." Hill explained that residents previously tried to approach trespassers directly about the property boundary, but encounters became confrontational. Now residents contact police when they witness unauthorized parking and foot traffic on their land. The clear visual marker that a fence once provided helped residents and visitors understand where private property began.

Not all beachgoers acknowledge the extent of the problem. Michael House, who regularly walks to JB-7 from a nearby public parking lot, said he has not witnessed the trespassing issues residents describe. "There's plenty of free parking. If they're damaging property and you know littering and stuff like that might be a different issue," House said. "I have never noticed anyone hopping the fence or the shrubs or anything like that."

The issue reached the Juno Beach Town Council, where officials noted the town has no legal obligation to install a fence. However, Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring a more affordable solution. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. The council decided to address the fence question during budget discussions scheduled for July 15. Hill expressed hope that the town will restore the barrier, saying residents want to protect their landscaping and parking spaces from continued trespassing.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League and was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. City leaders presented Riviera Beach's efforts to strengthen community engagement at the National Civic League conference in Denver, where judges announced the city as a first-time winner.

Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson credited the city's long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council for high school civic leadership, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98% completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program providing mini-grants to homeowners. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award reflects years of work focused on improving civic health and strengthening trust between residents and local government. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to represent Florida in National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade and will represent the entire state of Florida.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned an invitation to march in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade on July 4 at 10:30 a.m., representing Florida in the prestigious event. The students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to participate in this event.

Junior Lola Cabezas said millions, if not billions, of people will be watching the parade. Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is focused on nailing every detail of the marching and timing. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone said she has full confidence the students will put their best foot forward and represent the country well. Senior Lily Schaffer said getting to participate in the parade is an amazing opportunity that shows how much the program has grown. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those who want to watch from home.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
cards.teaser: For the third year in a row, the School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state, with 143 district-operated schools rated A or B.
cards.body:
For the third consecutive year, the School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. School districts and schools receive letter grades based on several factors, including student performance on state tests, graduation rates and student performance on advanced coursework. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, were rated "A" or "B," up from 120 schools the previous year. The district set a record with a 93.5% graduation rate, and 86% of seniors participated in college-level coursework, taking at least one Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment course. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

One of the biggest success stories came from S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach, which made a dramatic leap from a "C" rating last year to an "A" this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has spent the last 15 years as principal, said the school had an "A" rating two years ago and narrowly missed a "B" rating last year by just a few points. Three years ago, staff began modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" rating to an "A" this year, along with Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé Mark. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants and playing piano, and said she was always the first to lend a hand and loved kids and people. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, having previously lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. White's birthday is the Fourth of July, so she passed just a few days before her birthday.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after Anthem denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers investigational with insufficient proof that it improves health. GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the product's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and believes it is less risky than other options with proven success. Billington has been a vocal critic of insurance denials and recently shared Clark's denial on social media. Last year, after investigative reporting shared breast cancer patients' stories of denial, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark had her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago, thanks to Billington finding a mechanism to make it happen. Clark and Billington are continuing to fight the denial.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire days before her birthday
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a fire at her Hobe Sound home that investigators believe was caused by an electrical issue. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed the couple's belongings.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound. The blaze destroyed much of the residence, and preliminary findings from the sheriff's office suggest an electrical issue may have caused the fire. Authorities continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deadly incident.

White's fiancé Mark learned of her death and has since received support from the community. Friends launched a fundraiser to help him rebuild after losing many of his and White's belongings in the fire. This loss carries additional weight for Mark, who previously experienced the tragic death of his only child, Jacob. Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, has been working to support Mark during this difficult time. "I just am trying whatever I can to support him," Fenn said.

Fenn spoke about White's character and the kind of person she was. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano," Fenn said. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." Those who knew White remembered her as someone with a good soul who was always willing to help others. Fenn said White's memory will continue to live on in the hearts of those who loved her, noting that "She'll always be in our hearts."

The timing of White's death compounds the tragedy for her loved ones. Her birthday was July 4th, meaning she passed away just days before the holiday. Fenn reflected on this heartbreaking detail, saying "Misty's birthday is the Fourth of July. So, she passed just a few days before her birthday." The combination of losing White and the proximity to what should have been a celebration makes the loss particularly difficult for those in her life. As investigators continue their work, the community has rallied around Mark to help him move forward after this devastating loss.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk social media post
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court motion Thursday challenging an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a Spectrum Academy teacher su.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with his comments, which labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. After the judge's recommendation, Theobald told WPTV the case raises a larger question about where the line is drawn for teachers speaking outside of school. The school board still has the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back.

Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Without it, only bushes separate the public access path from private land. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer with cars parking on private spots and people pushing through bushes with coolers, fishing rods and lawn chairs. Hill said residents used to confront trespassers but now call police because people became rude.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved giving 7 acres of land to FDOT for a partial Turnpike interchange as the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project continues. The interchange aims to fill a significant gap between Turnpike entrances in the city.
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. Samples said the interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth anticipated over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety concerns. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road remains in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: California company proposes elevated self-driving network linking West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways will present to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday a proposal for autonomous electric vehicles on an elevated guideway connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The trip could take less than 10 minutes.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The company will present the proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, bypassing traffic congestion entirely. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

The system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system, according to Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger, who referenced previous South Florida light rail discussions that carried estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Tuesday's County Commission meeting will determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal, not approve construction. If commissioners move forward, the county could seek competing bids and begin deeper discussions on routes, station locations, costs and financing. Gettinger said the service would be priced like public transit rather than rideshare and would require local employees to staff operations centers and maintenance facilities.

hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.
hero.body:
Riviera Beach has earned a major national distinction, becoming the only Florida community selected for the 2026 All-America City Award. The city is one of just 10 U.S. communities to receive this honor from the National Civic League. The award was announced at the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented information about the city's community engagement efforts. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, describing Riviera Beach as "one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." He noted that the award reflects years of dedicated work to revitalize the city and enhance quality of life for residents.

The All-America City Award recognizes communities that unite residents, government, businesses and organizations to address local problems and create meaningful change. City leaders said the recognition reflects a long-term commitment to improving civic health, building trust between residents and local government, and giving the community a direct role in shaping the city's future. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson emphasized that the award belongs to the entire community. "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents," she said. "Every event we host, every project we complete, and every challenge we overcome happens because our community shows up for one another."

Riviera Beach's application highlighted three key programs that promote civic participation and neighborhood investment. The Riviera Beach Youth Council engages high school students in civic leadership and advocacy. The Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education program, achieved a 98 percent completion rate. The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program offers mini-grants to longtime homeowners for necessary repairs. Miller-Anderson explained that these initiatives represent a broader commitment to treating civic engagement as an ongoing partnership between government, residents, faith groups, schools and community organizations. "We're doing a lot of innovative things to make sure that our community is able to say that they are part of what's happening here in the city," she said.

The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors. City leaders say the designation celebrates Riviera Beach's progress and positions the community for future opportunities and growth. The award sends a message to the nation that Riviera Beach is a place where collaboration produces results and residents actively shape the community's future. Miller-Anderson added that winning the award reinforces positive momentum. "Winning this brings back community pride," she said.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year as ground beef and strawberry prices rise
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82 according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, up 4% from a year ago.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points squarely at inflation as the cause. Ground beef is up 5.5%, and buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream is up 5.3%.

Not everything is more expensive, though. Potato prices are down this year, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch said families can keep costs in check by shopping savvier than ever, comparing stores to see who has the best deals for groceries on their list, and cutting down on food waste by starting with a meal plan.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied insurance coverage hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, and her surgeon are speaking out after her insurance company Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and chose to have a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurer, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which is still considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body, but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Despite the denial, Clark had her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago, thanks to her plastic surgeon, Dr. Alicia Billington. Billington uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product is giving her patients the least amount of complications. Clark and Billington are still fighting the denial. Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield said it regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they're based on medical evidence and aligned with the latest treatment standards, but the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights recommendation to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is contesting a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy who has worked there since 2009. Theobald was suspended following Facebook comments labeling Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation, claiming "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney maintains that Theobald's Facebook post constituted a "serious offense" and that his removal was appropriate.

Last month, Livingstone issued an order recommending Theobald's reinstatement, citing a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that found disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violated First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald receive back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald acknowledged writing the comments but stated they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority to decide whether Theobald returns to his position.

cards.headline: Boca Raton High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade on July 4, representing the entire state of Florida.
cards.body:
On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the Boca Raton Community High School band will march a full mile along the National Mall in Washington, D.C., from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue, representing Florida at the National Independence Day Parade. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event. Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the scale of the audience, saying "There are millions, if not billions, of people watching. It's a lot of pressure, but I think we'll be able to rise to the occasion." She explained the physical demands of marching band, noting that musicians must play, breathe, and walk while maintaining consistent sound without hearing their footsteps in the music.

Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is focused on executing every detail perfectly. "Just focusing on the marching, the timing of everything. Everybody is going to be able to see it. Everyone will be able to see what the Boca High band is capable of," Restivo said. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed confidence in her students, saying she has "full confidence in our students that they'll put their best foot forward, literally, and we'll rise to the occasion and represent our country well." Senior Lily Schaffer called the opportunity amazing, saying it "shows how much we've grown and showcases what we do here." The parade will be streamed live on YouTube.

hero.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
hero.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is preparing for the 2026 fall season with ambitious goals after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district championship. Despite their successful regular season, a second-round playoff loss has motivated the program to aim higher this year, with a state title now in their sights.

Head coach Jimmy Robertson credits the team's veteran leadership as a driving force behind their championship aspirations. He noted that most of the seniors have been with the program for four years and came through the middle school ranks, giving them deep knowledge of how the program operates. According to Robertson, "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had." This continuity and experience has created high expectations for the upcoming campaign.

The Scots are taking deliberate steps to strengthen their program by scheduling more challenging opponents this fall. Senior Jack Williams explained that the team wants to compete at a higher level and attract attention by facing strong teams. "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. So we really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete. That's what we wanna do and we wanna take that next level, and it's by playing against really good teams that we do that and attract new people," Williams said. This strategic approach reflects the team's commitment to building momentum for the postseason.

The Scots are measuring success by a single metric: advancing further in the playoffs. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that regular season accomplishments matter less than postseason performance. "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs. We just gotta go farther than that, that's all that matters," Whelche said. To prepare for their goals, the team is grinding through summer workouts. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily training builds motivation for the season ahead, noting "It just adds up every day as something like to look forward to. Work harder so we can see the results when we come off the season positive and break our record." With experienced leadership and focused preparation, the Scots believe they have the tools to achieve a championship run.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams prepare for Fourth of July boating surge
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats with medics on standby as hundreds of boaters take to local waterways for the holiday weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected to hit Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend, prompting Martin County Maritime Response Unit to prepare for the surge. Lt. Brett Harry said his team will station two boats with medics on standby in the north and south areas of Martin County to assist anyone in need. Harry noted the unit is prepared to handle everything from minor injuries like stubbed toes to serious medical emergencies including cardiac events and potential spinal injuries.

Harry urged boaters to take safety precautions by keeping their eyes on the water, designating a sober driver, and packing life vests, whistles and flotation devices. Among those preparing for the holiday weekend are boaters Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched Friday from Sandsprit Park in Martin County with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons said safety is their top priority when heading out on the water to celebrate.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board challenges judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The school board is fighting a judge's recommendation to give Matt Theobald his job back at Spectrum Academy after he was suspended for Facebook comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, was suspended last year after making social media comments labeling Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone recommended last month that Theobald be reinstated with back pay and benefits. In her order, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights.

In a Thursday court filing, the Martin County School Board challenged the judge's recommendation, arguing that numerous findings in the order are not based on competent substantial evidence. The board's attorney contended that Theobald's Facebook post was a serious offense and that removing him was appropriate. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view. The school board retains the final decision on whether Theobald returns to his teaching position.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community supports man who lost fiancee in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a fire at her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed their belongings.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help White's fiancé Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, said she learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. "It's just a terrible shame and awful loss of life," Fenn said. Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing piano. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people," Fenn said. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. Fenn said Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. White's death is especially painful for those who knew her because her birthday is July 4, meaning she passed just days before the holiday.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient's insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark's insurance company Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before it was scheduled, citing concerns about the surgical mesh treatment.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She chose a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction to eliminate any possibility of recurrence. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. The denial letter stated the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered investigational with no or not enough proof it improves health. GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction.

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it gives patients the least amount of complications compared to other options. Clark received her reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after Billington found a way to make it happen. An Anthem spokesperson said the company regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and that GalaFlex does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by their medical policy. Last year, Cigna became the first major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Clark and Billington are still fighting the denial.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed and roof fixed after WPTV investigation
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his roof but was left with unfinished work and a nearly $7,000 lien on his home.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, paid Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach more than $17,000 to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof ahead of hurricane season. McCoy said he was mostly satisfied with the work except for two holes left unfinished on the back side of his home. After the company stopped responding to his calls, texts and emails beginning in January, McCoy received letters from Gulfeagle Supply warning that the company had filed a nearly $7,000 lien on his home. The lien document stated that Gulfeagle Supply had furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing for McCoy's property but was not paid for those supplies. McCoy said he worried he would have to hire an attorney or go to court.

After WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke with the Seabreeze Roofing owner, a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized was delivered to McCoy within an hour. Crews returned to McCoy's roof to finish the job about an hour after he received the waiver. McCoy said the experience had been a burden and expressed his relief at the resolution.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was selected as one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League.
cards.body:
The National Civic League announced Riviera Beach as a 2026 All-America City Award winner during its conference in Denver, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Riviera Beach was one of 10 U.S. communities to receive the award, which has been presented annually since 1949.

Mayor Douglas Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. Riviera Beach's application highlighted the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program providing mini-grants to longtime homeowners. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award reflects years of work focused on improving civic health and strengthening trust between residents and local government.

hero.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and pool party at country club
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting season programs through September
cards.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. The center's offerings include guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, these programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Florida Lt. Governor's wife of running anonymous attack accounts
hero.body:
Two veteran communications staffers from Governor Ron DeSantis's administration have publicly alleged that Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, operated anonymous social media accounts to promote her husband's gubernatorial campaign while attacking the governor. Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both presented evidence linking the accounts to the Second Lady. The accounts were deactivated shortly after the accusations became public.

Pushaw shared information from Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing that the X account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email address similar to ones associated with Layla Collins. Florida Politics verified the connection through screenshots of two-factor authentication messages, which were triggered when someone attempted to access the account without the correct password. The screenshots displayed authentication messages sent to an email address with letters obscured and a phone number showing only the final digits. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said also appeared connected to Layla Collins. According to Pushaw, the account's posts consisted entirely of promoting Jay Collins and attacking individuals who refused to endorse him, including the governor.

Redfern corroborated the allegation, stating that "the FSUDude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number." Both accounts were deactivated after the two men publicly criticized them. Pushaw noted the apparent contradiction in Layla Collins serving on a state board appointed by the same governor whose account had called a coward. She questioned how someone with such important state duties would have time to maintain and post on multiple burner accounts so frequently. In her own posts, Pushaw emphasized that beyond the communication links, the account's content pattern suggested it existed primarily to advance her husband's political ambitions. "Account content is entirely comprised of two types of posts: Promoting Jay Collins, and attacking people who didn't endorse Jay, including the governor," Pushaw stated.

DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year, positioning the former state Senator to develop a statewide political profile. The governor has not endorsed a preferred candidate in the upcoming gubernatorial race and cannot seek a third term due to term limits. Redfern currently works for Attorney General James Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for governor. Florida Politics requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins regarding the allegations.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Cord Byrd moves to keep St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark off ballot
cards.teaser: Five state employees gave sworn declarations that Paula Stark's treasurer never submitted required Form 6 paperwork before the June 12 qualifying deadline.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking Leon Circuit Court to keep St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark off the ballot, arguing she failed to submit required Form 6 paperwork before the June 12 deadline. Five state employees submitted sworn written declarations stating that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted Form 6 nor received it back when he submitted remaining paperwork in the final 30 minutes before the noon deadline. Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve said Stark was one of 12 candidates who did not properly turn in Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests. Half of those candidates corrected their problems and qualified. Three weeks after the deadline passed, Stark still has not submitted the form.

Reeve also cited Stark's history of paperwork violations, including a campaign finance report filed over one month late, reported excessive contributions, and an incorrect address on file. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. If Stark is removed from the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 will feature Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves with no other Republican candidates, though the district traditionally leans Democratic and covers Osceola and Orange counties. Byrd noted that ballots must be mailed to overseas military by July 4 and vote-by-mail ballots must be sent out July 9-16.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion plan to redevelop Tropicana Field site
cards.teaser: Mayor Ken Welch selected The Burg Bid proposal, which centers on a 13-acre civic park, the Woodson African American Museum, and 3,600 income-restricted housing units.
cards.body:
St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch selected The Burg Bid as the city's preferred path forward for redeveloping Tropicana Field and the Historic Gas Plant District. Led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, the $8.1 billion proposal calls for purchasing 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, with the team valuing the full land package at $405 million when factoring in $130 million in land the city would retain. The proposal includes a $20 million deposit when a purchase and sale agreement is executed.

The plan centers on Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre civic and cultural space that would anchor the district and include The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a planned Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad, cafe areas, public art and a concert lawn. The Woodson would sit within Samuel Davis Park along a diagonal pedestrian corridor called the Legacy Link. The proposal also includes 3,600 income-restricted housing units over a 15-year buildout, with 1,800 units in the Historic Gas Plant District and 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. The district would be built in three phases, each expected to take about five years, with early development potentially beginning before stadium demolition. The team's lease with the city ends after the 2028 season.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire days before her birthday
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a fire at her Hobe Sound home. The Martin County Sheriff's Office preliminary findings point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home she shared with her fiancé. Preliminary findings from the Martin County Sheriff's Office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The investigation into the fire remains ongoing.

Nina Fenn, who had been friends with White for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé Mark. According to Fenn, the flames destroyed many of the couple's belongings, leaving them in what she described as "a state of devastation." In response to the loss, friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the fire.

Fenn spoke about White's character and the impact she had on those around her. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano," Fenn said. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." Fenn emphasized that White will be remembered for her generosity and kindness to others.

The timing of White's death has added to the heartbreak felt by those who knew her. White's birthday was July 4, meaning she passed away just days before turning another year older. The loss is also compounded by tragedy Mark has already endured in his life. Fenn noted that Mark lost his only child, Jacob, in a previous tragedy. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically," Fenn said. "So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him." For Fenn and others in the community, White's memory will continue to live on. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit deployed two boats with medics on standby Friday as hundreds of boaters launched into waterways for Fourth of July weekend .

hero.headline: Body of missing diver recovered near Fort Pierce Inlet
hero.teaser: The body of a missing diver was found on the Florida coast near Fort Pierce Inlet, according to deputies.
hero.body:
St. Lucie County deputies reported the recovery of a missing diver's body near Fort Pierce Inlet on the Florida coast. The discovery was made after the diver had been reported missing.

Deputies are handling the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the diver's death. The recovery took place along the Fort Pierce Inlet area.

cards.headline: Driver held teens at gunpoint after Orbeez pellet shooting in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: A driver held teenagers at gunpoint after they shot Orbeez pellets at his car in Port St. Lucie, according to police.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police reported an incident in which a driver held teenagers at gunpoint following an altercation involving Orbeez pellets. The teens had shot Orbeez pellets at the driver's car before the confrontation occurred.

The incident highlights ongoing issues with Orbeez pellet shootings in the area. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the gunpoint confrontation.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with $95 million Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, there is a significant gap between the Turnpike's current entrances and exits in the city. The interchange is designed to improve accessibility and accommodate growth projected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, both still in design phases. The project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land to FDOT at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Two people rescued after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: Two people were rescued after their boat sank in the Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County.
cards.body:
Rescue crews responded to a boat sinking in the Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County and successfully rescued two people. The boat went down in the waterway, prompting an emergency response.

Bodycam footage captured the rescue operation as crews worked to pull the two individuals from the water. Both people were safely rescued from the sinking vessel.

cards.headline: Costco planning first Treasure Coast location in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: Costco is planning to open its first Treasure Coast store in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie will be home to the first Costco warehouse store on the Treasure Coast. The retail giant is moving forward with plans to establish a location in the city.

The new Costco would be the first for the three-county Treasure Coast region. Port St. Lucie continues to attract major retailers as the city experiences population growth.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman recognized for supporting little free libraries
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce woman has been recognized for her support of little free libraries in the community.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce resident received recognition for her work supporting little free libraries throughout the area. The woman has contributed to maintaining and promoting these community book-sharing stations.

Little free libraries provide residents with access to books through neighborhood installations. The Fort Pierce woman's efforts have helped sustain these resources in the community.

cards.headline: Legacy Lions Football standings updated for Port St. Lucie high school
cards.teaser: The Legacy Lions Football team in Port St. Lucie has updated standings released.
cards.body:
Legacy Lions Football in Port St. Lucie has updated team standings available. The high school football program continues its season with current records published.

The Legacy Lions represent Port St. Lucie in high school football competition. Team standings are tracked throughout the season.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast communities plan events for 250th anniversary of American independence
hero.teaser: Communities across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beaches are preparing special celebrations to mark the 250th anniversary of American independence today.
hero.body:
Cities and towns in the Treasure Coast region are hosting events Saturday to commemorate the semiquincentennial of the United States. The milestone 250th anniversary of independence falls on July 4, 2026.

Communities in Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties are participating in the celebrations alongside neighboring Palm Beach County. The anniversary marks 250 years since the Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.

The semiquincentennial represents a once-in-a-lifetime observance for residents across the region. Local governments and community groups have organized special programs for the historic occasion.

cards.headline: Travel + Leisure highlights Treasure Coast town as favorite Florida destination
cards.teaser: A national travel magazine has spotlighted a Treasure Coast community as a top Florida destination after more than 20 years of visits.
cards.body:
A national travel magazine has spotlighted a Treasure Coast community as a top Florida destination after more than 20 years of visits. Travel + Leisure published a feature Friday highlighting the town's combination of uncrowded beaches and a lively arts scene.

The publication cited the area's arts community and beach access as standout features that distinguish it from more crowded Florida coastal destinations. The recognition comes during the busy summer tourist season along the Treasure Coast.

The feature focuses on the town's cultural offerings alongside its natural attractions. Travel + Leisure has featured destinations across Florida for decades, making the specific callout of a Treasure Coast location notable for the region's tourism industry.

The article appeared online Friday as travelers plan Fourth of July weekend trips and summer vacations. The Treasure Coast encompasses Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties along Florida's Atlantic coast between Palm Beach and Brevard counties.

cards.headline: Fireworks displays scheduled across Treasure Coast for Fourth of July
cards.teaser: Multiple fireworks shows are planned across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beaches for the Fourth of July holiday.
cards.body:
Communities throughout the Treasure Coast region have scheduled fireworks displays for Independence Day celebrations Saturday. The shows are part of Fourth of July festivities in Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

The fireworks displays are scheduled in various Treasure Coast locations alongside neighboring Palm Beach County communities. Residents can attend multiple shows across the region for the holiday weekend.

The Fourth of July fireworks represent annual Independence Day traditions for Treasure Coast communities. This year's celebrations coincide with the 250th anniversary of American independence.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year as inflation affects holiday spending
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July cookout for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from last year, according to a new survey tracking holiday meal expenses.
cards.body:
The American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey found that a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. Inflation is the primary driver behind the rising costs for traditional Independence Day foods. Ground beef prices are up 5.5%, and buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream is up 5.3%. Potato prices are down this year, offering relief for potato chip and salad shoppers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends families keep costs in check by shopping strategically. She said it's important to compare stores to find the best deals for groceries on your list. Woroch also emphasized that the biggest thing families can do is cut down on food waste, which begins with creating a meal plan.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, and her surgeon are criticizing Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield after the insurer denied coverage for reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy followed by reconstruction surgery. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction procedure, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the surgery, which involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex. According to the denial letter, the surgery is considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." The FDA has not approved GalaFlex for breast reconstruction and considers it an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that GalaFlex's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it gives patients the least amount of complications compared to other options. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after Billington found a way to make it happen. Anthem said the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" but noted the company covers many other evidence-based alternatives. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction following an investigative series. Clark and Billington continue fighting the denial.

cards.headline: Boca Raton High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march in Washington D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade today, representing the entire state of Florida.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing Florida on one of America's most famous streets. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event.

Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the scale of the performance, saying "There are millions, if not billions, of people watching." She also explained the physical demands of marching band, noting that students must play, breathe, and walk while maintaining consistent sound. Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is focused on timing and execution, adding that "Everyone will be able to see what the Boca High band is capable of." Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed confidence in her students, saying she has "full confidence in our students that they'll put their best foot forward, literally, and we'll rise to the occasion and represent our country well." Senior Lily Schaffer called the opportunity amazing, saying it "shows how much we've grown and showcases what we do here." The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for remote viewers.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's football team targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.teaser: The Saint Andrew's Scots finished last season 10-2 with a district title but are pushing for more after a second-round playoff exit.
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are preparing for the 2026 fall football season with their focus on winning a state title. Last season, the team finished with a 10-2 record and won a district championship, but a second-round playoff exit left them believing more was possible. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson highlighted the strength of the senior class, noting that most are four-year seniors who came up through the middle school program and have experienced success throughout their careers. To elevate the program, Saint Andrew's has scheduled more challenging opponents this fall to compete at the next level and attract new players.

The Scots are measuring success this season by postseason advancement. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that while an undefeated regular season is desired, it means nothing if the team continues losing in the second round of playoffs. The team must advance further in the postseason to consider the season an improvement. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily summer workouts serve as motivation to break the team's record when the season begins. With a veteran senior class leading the way, the program is embracing the grind of summer training as preparation for their championship run.
